gaps.what: An enum with associated values isn't `Codable` by itself: give a saved enum raw values (`enum Priority: String, Codable`), or write its `init(from:)` and `encode(to:)`.
A tuple doesn't take its labels from the declared type: write them in the literal (`return (min: a, max: b)`).

symbols.name: UnsafeContinuation
symbols.notes: The same as `CheckedContinuation` in Kiln.

symbols.name: UserDefaults
symbols.notes: The app's own settings: `standard` is the app's suite, which its `@AppStorage` shares.

symbols.name: AngularGradient
symbols.notes: Colors only: `stops:` aren't placed.

symbols.name: ArrangementView
symbols.notes: A primary and a secondary view, split or overlaid by `.arrangementViewStyle(.split)` or `.overlay`.

symbols.name: ButtonBorderShape
symbols.notes: Its members as a shape (`ButtonBorderShape.capsule`), filled with the foreground style; use `Capsule()` to `.fill` or `.stroke` one.

symbols.name: Canvas
symbols.notes: Draws nothing yet: draw with a custom `Shape` instead.

symbols.name: Chart
symbols.notes: Bar, line, point, area, sector and rule marks, by value or by series; the axes and the legend can be hidden.

symbols.name: Color
symbols.notes: Named and system colors, `Color(red:green:blue:)`, `Color(hue:…)`, `Color(white:)`, hex strings, and `.opacity`.

symbols.name: DatePicker
symbols.notes: `displayedComponents` `.date`, `.hourAndMinute` or both, with an `in:` range (`date...`, `...date` or `a...b`); every style, `.graphical` included.

symbols.name: EditableCollectionContent
symbols.notes: What `ForEach($items, editActions:)` makes.

symbols.name: EllipticalGradient
symbols.notes: Colors only: `stops:` aren't placed.

symbols.name: EquatableView
symbols.notes: Shows its content; Kiln redraws it with its parent.

symbols.name: ForEach
symbols.notes: Over arrays, ranges and bindings (`ForEach($items) { $item in }`), by `id:` or `Identifiable`.

symbols.name: GeometryReader
symbols.notes: The closure gets a `GeometryProxy`: `size`, `safeAreaInsets`, `frame(in:)`, `bounds(of:)`.

symbols.name: GroupElementsOfContent
symbols.notes: What `Group(subviews:transform:)` makes.

symbols.name: GroupSectionsOfContent
symbols.notes: What `Group(sections:transform:)` makes.

symbols.name: Image
symbols.notes: SF Symbols (`systemName:`), the host's images by name; other assets show a placeholder.

symbols.name: LinearGradient
symbols.notes: Colors only: `stops:` aren't placed.

symbols.name: List
symbols.notes: Rows, sections, `ForEach` with `onDelete` and `onMove`; `selection:` one value (an optional) or a `Set` (with `EditButton`); `children:` for an outline.

symbols.name: MultiDatePicker
symbols.notes: `selection` is a `Set<DateComponents>`; read `.year`, `.month` and `.day` from each.

symbols.name: NavigationSplitView
symbols.notes: Two or three columns on iPad; on iPhone it's a stack from the sidebar. `columnVisibility:` and `preferredCompactColumn:` are kept.

symbols.name: NavigationStack
symbols.notes: Push with `NavigationLink(value:)` and `.navigationDestination(for:)`; `path:` is an array of values or a `NavigationPath`.

symbols.name: OutlineGroup
symbols.notes: Over a tree: `OutlineGroup(items, children: \.children) { item in … }`, with `id:` or `Identifiable` items.

symbols.name: OutlineSubgroupChildren
symbols.notes: The children an `OutlineGroup` shows under a row.

symbols.name: Path
symbols.notes: `move(to:)`, lines, arcs, curves, rects and ellipses; a `Path` in a body is drawn like a shape.

symbols.name: Picker
symbols.notes: Rows are tagged with `.tag`, or by their `ForEach` id.

symbols.name: ProgressView
symbols.notes: Indeterminate, `value:total:`, `timerInterval:countsDown:`, or your own `ProgressViewStyle`.

symbols.name: RadialGradient
symbols.notes: Colors only: `stops:` aren't placed.

symbols.name: RenameButton
symbols.notes: Runs the nearest `.renameAction { }`.

symbols.name: ScrollViewReader
symbols.notes: `proxy.scrollTo(id, anchor:)`.

symbols.name: ShareLink
symbols.notes: Shows its label; sharing isn't wired up yet.

symbols.name: Slider
symbols.notes: Labels, `step:`, `neutralValue:`, `enabledBounds:`, and tick marks (`ticks: { SliderTick(0.5) }`, iOS 26).

symbols.name: Subview
symbols.notes: A resolved subview: show it, modify it, and read `id` and `containerValues`.

symbols.name: SubviewsCollection
symbols.notes: `Group(subviews:)`'s subviews: an array you can count, index, slice and `ForEach` over.

symbols.name: SubviewsCollectionSlice
symbols.notes: A slice of the subviews (`subviews.prefix(3)`, `subviews.dropFirst()`).

symbols.name: TabView
symbols.notes: `Tab`s (with `value:`, `role: .search`) and `TabSection`s, or views with `.tabItem`; `selection:` is the tab's value.

symbols.name: Text
symbols.notes: Strings, `verbatim:`, `format:`, and dates with `style:`. A literal's numbers are formatted as SwiftUI does.

overloads.notes: A live countdown or count-up over a `start...end` range of dates.

symbols.name: TextEditor
symbols.notes: Bound to a `String`, or to an `AttributedString` (iOS 26), which keeps its styling. `selection:` isn't kept.

symbols.name: TextField
symbols.notes: `text:`, or `value:format:` with `.number`, `.currency(code:)` or `.percent`; `axis: .vertical` grows. `selection:` isn't kept.

symbols.name: TextInputBorderShape
symbols.notes: For `.textInputBorderShape(_:)`: `.capsule`, `.roundedRectangle` or `.automatic`.

symbols.name: TimelineView
symbols.notes: `.periodic(from:by:)` and `.everyMinute`; the closure gets `context.date`.

symbols.name: AppStorage
symbols.notes: Kept per app.

symbols.name: Environment
symbols.notes: The key paths listed as environment values; not `@Environment(Model.self)`.

symbols.name: EnvironmentObject
symbols.notes: Set with `.environmentObject(_:)`.

symbols.name: FocusState
symbols.notes: Holds a value; it doesn't move the keyboard focus yet.

symbols.name: FocusedValue
symbols.notes: Reads its `@Entry` default; focused views don't set it yet.

symbols.name: ScaledMetric
symbols.notes: Scaled for the text size when the view first appears; it doesn't follow a later change of Dynamic Type.

symbols.name: SceneStorage
symbols.notes: Kept while the app is open.

symbols.name: State
symbols.notes: Lives as long as the view, by SwiftUI's own identity rules.

wontDo.reason: Too much for the value. Geocoding stays (§4.6).
A live preview layer and session management; `UIImagePickerController` covers taking a photo (§4.3).
They need a compiled Metal library, and run off the main thread at frame rate.
`DB` is the synced store.
Apps run only while their card is open.
A Shelf app is one screen inside a card. `WindowGroup` stays: it's the app's root.
wontDo.what: iOS 27's `Document` protocol, documents, multiple windows and scenes, commands

wontDo.reason: Each controller is bridged on purpose, and the app delegate is Shelf's.
Entitlements, or delegate-heavy APIs for little use here.
On PLAN.md's Later list.
Purchases need App Store products and an app record; Shelf apps aren't sold through the App Store.
They need a merchant ID, pass type IDs and entitlements that Shelf can't grant per app.
Scene graphs of subclassed native nodes, run at frame rate; see subclassing native classes. `Canvas` and `TimelineView` cover 2D games.
wontDo.what: RealityKit, SceneKit and SpriteKit views, game controllers

wontDo.reason: MusicKit is registered per bundle ID, so every app would share Shelf's.
wontDo.what: MusicKit views (`ArtworkImage`, the music picker, subscription offer)

wontDo.reason: Needs an entitlement and server-side token checks per app.
Entitlement-gated, or they register the app with the system, which a Shelf app can't do.
wontDo.what: Siri and Shortcuts views, Screen Time, managed apps, PermissionKit, device discovery, screen capture

wontDo.reason: There's no canvas in Shelf; `#Preview` blocks are skipped when read (§1.6).
SwiftUI keeps their requirements private (`_makeView`, `_body`), so no app can adopt them, compiled or not. The built-in styles all work.
On iPhone a `Table` collapses to its first column with no headers, so it's a `List` that's harder to write; use a `List` of rows, or a `Grid` for columns.
It hands the app `NSItemProvider`s from a drag, which arrive with drag and drop (§4.1).
SwiftUI calls its static `height(in:)` while it lays out the sheet, off the main actor, where Kiln's code can't run; `.fraction(_:)` and `.height(_:)` cover the same sizes.
It binds a `TextSelection`, which arrives with text selection in Sharing (§3.2).
wontDo.what: `.searchSelection(_:)`: the selected range in the search field
